Level 1 · Introduction · Week 10

Random Art and My Own Commands

random makes surprises; def makes your own command, just like My Blocks.

What you will learn

  • How to make your own command with def, with input slots called parameters.
  • The difference between defining a command and calling (using) it.
  • How random makes a new picture every time you press Run.
  • How to plan your final project: My Interactive Art Show.

The big idea: make your own command

In Scratch you made My Blocks. Python has them too! You write def, a name, and the input slots in brackets.

→ 
def flower(x, y, color):
    t.penup()
    t.goto(x, y)
    t.pendown()
    t.color(color)
    ...

Defining writes the recipe. Nothing is drawn yet! Calling uses the recipe. The values in the brackets go into the slots, in order:

TipRemember

Define first (at the top), call later (at the bottom). Calls start at the left edge — not pushed in — or they become part of the recipe.

Exercise10.1: Flower Stamp

Folder: week10/ex-flower-stamp. Run the starter: nothing is drawn! The recipe is there, but nobody calls it.

  1. At the bottom, call it three times: flower(-200, 0), flower(0, 0), flower(200, 0).

  2. Add a third parameter: def flower(x, y, color): and use t.color(color).

  3. Give each call a color: flower(-200, 0, PALETTE[0]), and so on.

Done looks like: three flowers in different colors, each with a yellow middle.

Surprise! The random module

random.randint(1, 6) Like rolling a dice: a whole number from 1 to 6.
random.randint(-350, 350) A random spot from left (-350) to right (350).
random.choice(PALETTE) Like picking a crayon from a bag with your eyes closed.

Put import random at the top of your program, next to import turtle.

Exercise10.2: Random Bubble Art

Folder: week10/ex-random-art. The starter draws 30 bubbles… all in the same place! Inside the loop, change the fixed numbers to random ones: x, y, size with random.randint, and color with random.choice(PALETTE). Press Run three times. Is it different each time?

Your final project: My Interactive Art Show

For weeks 10 to 12 you will make your own program for an art show. It says hello, asks the viewer one or two questions, and draws a picture that changes because of the answers. It must use these six ingredients:

Ideas: a fish party under the sea, a garden of flowers, a city skyline at night, space with planets, a birthday card, a pattern machine. Write three ideas you like:

Then fill in the plan sheet in your Project Brief (Milestone M1): a sketch, your questions, and your function’s name and inputs.

TipBe an original artist

Borrowing an idea is fine when you make it your own and say thank you. Write a comment like # Flower idea remixed from Exercise 10.1. Questions in your project ask about choices — colors, numbers, day or night — never about who someone is.

Reflect

What command would you like to invent for your project? What would its input slots be?

Why do you think a function is useful when you need ten flowers?

New words

Function
A command you make yourself, with a name. Like a My Block.
def
The Python word that starts a function’s recipe: def flower(x, y, color): .
Parameter
An input slot of a function, like x , y or color .
Call
Using a function: flower(0, 0, "#CC79A7") .
random
A Python toolbox for surprises: randint and choice .
Remix
Making something new from someone’s idea, and giving them credit.
